item.title: Value and certainty are shaping UK travel bookings this August. Three data points agents within JLT can put to work this week.
item.description:
Value and certainty are shaping UK travel bookings this August. Three data points agents within JLT can put to work this week.
- Egypt arrivals rose 7% in the first four months of 2026. North Africa is the value answer when a Caribbean budget doesn't stretch. - Late fly-cruise bookings are up 13% year-on-year. Warm leads who've been searching are ready for a direct nudge. - 76% of August UK bookings were four or five star, driven by all-inclusive certainty. Lead with the all-in price, not the star rating.
The full trend breakdown is on the blog this week, including ready-to-use prompts for your next enquiry.

item.title: The travel market is moving fast this summer, and four trends this week point toward agents.
item.description:
The travel market is moving fast this summer, and four trends this week point toward agents.
For JLT agents, the key takeaways from this week's research:
- Last-minute summer is real: next-day sun bookings are up 26% year on year, with Mallorca, Tenerife and Ibiza leading demand - September is the shoulder-season opportunity to pitch now, before the best value disappears - Confidence in booking through a travel professional reached 41% this year, up from 36%, with ease of booking (57%) and time saved (42%) as the top reasons people choose an agent over doing it themselves
Our weekly trending blog breaks down all four trends and the booking angles behind each.
Blog link in first comment: https://janinelovestravel.co.uk/whats-trending-in-travel-last-minute-sun-2026-08-20

item.title: Short-haul sun is the dominant theme in travel search data this summer. The booking angles are clear.
item.description:
Short-haul sun is the dominant theme in travel search data this summer. The booking angles are clear.
Tripadvisor has named Alicante the No.1 trending European destination for UK travellers. Albania is in the top five. UK domestic is running behind overseas booking pace, with a late-booking window open for August and October half-term.
Three takeaways for agents this week:
- Short-haul sun is leading: Alicante, Malaga, Rhodes and Alvor all on the rise. Warm, close, and sorted is the brief. - Albania is gaining genuine traction as a value-led alternative. Ksamil and Himare are the destinations to know. - UK domestic is underbooked relative to overseas. Late-summer and half-term content has real timing on its side.
This week's trends blog has the full breakdown, with ready-to-use content hooks for each.

item.title: Demand data for 2026 is pointing in several directions at once. Agents who read the spread can benefit across a wide range of client types.
item.description:
Demand data for 2026 is pointing in several directions at once. Agents who read the spread can benefit across a wide range of client types.
Three takeaways from this week's trends:
- Japan is the No. 1 bucket-list destination for Brits in 2026. Thailand is the most searched. Build a comparison resource your clients can use. - Madeira topped Tripadvisor's global trending list. It is a strong alternative when clients ask for the Canaries or the Med. - UK staycations are up across the board, with North Wales leading and Herefordshire searches up 76%. Easy half-term bookings for the pipeline.

item.title: Booking behaviour is moving. Here is what the data shows for the week of 23 July 2026, and what it means for agents building their pipelines.
item.description:
Booking behaviour is moving. Here is what the data shows for the week of 23 July 2026, and what it means for agents building their pipelines.
Here's what to act on this week:
- Canary Islands last-minute bookings are up 142% year on year. Short-haul sun enquiries need a fast, confident response. - Cruise confidence is returning at pace. Annual bookings are up 21.6%, with expedition up 86% and luxury up 48%. The premium door is open. - September intent has climbed from 17% to 24% since 2023. The shoulder season window is building. Start the conversation while pricing is still favourable. - All-inclusive now makes up 37% of sales, up from 30% a year ago. Budget-nervous clients are choosing certainty.
Our agents get data like this every week, alongside the pitches to use with it. This is what being in JLT looks like.

item.title: Four separate travel trend reports this week, all pointing the same direction.
item.description:
Four separate travel trend reports this week, all pointing the same direction.
UK coastal searches are up 40%, cruise sales are up 21.6% year-on-year, and one in four UK travellers is now planning a September trip. The pattern is consistent: travellers want better value and are booking later. They are also more open to somewhere new than the data has reflected in some time.
For agents in JLT working with hesitant clients right now, three angles to lead with: - UK short breaks as a confident alternative to stalled long-haul plans - Cruise-and-stay combinations, which are outperforming solo sailings and building stronger bookings - September shoulder season, an opportunity that rewards agents who quote it before the summer rush closes in
Our full breakdown, with booking angles for each trend, is in this week's What's Trending blog.

item.title: UK travel in summer 2026 has a clear shape, and it's worth agents understanding what's driving it.
item.description:
UK travel in summer 2026 has a clear shape, and it's worth agents understanding what's driving it.
Domestic searches are up over 11% year on year. The average booked international trip sits around 317 miles from home. Cost of living is the primary planning factor for 42% of UK adults.
Three actions agents can take from this week's trending data:
- Shoulder season is the saving that costs clients nothing but flexibility. Push Autumn 2026 departures now, with a clear GBP£ comparison - Lead the property conversation. 27% of travellers now choose accommodation that is part of the experience itself, not a backdrop to it - Ask the multi-gen question on every family enquiry. 31% are travelling with extended family this year, and the right property for that group takes some finding
The full breakdown is in this week's What's Trending blog.
Blog link (first comment, once live): https://janinelovestravel.co.uk/whats-trending-in-travel-short-haul-shoulder-season-2026-07-02

item.title: UK travellers are not pulling back on summer 2026. They are making sharper choices about when, where and how they spend.
item.description:
UK travellers are not pulling back on summer 2026. They are making sharper choices about when, where and how they spend.
Three things our agents are working with this week:
- Date-shifting is real. Thirty-one percent of UK adults planning summer travel are choosing off-peak dates. Late August and early September represent strong value windows to present to families.
- Mountain and lake escapes are growing fast. Seventy-one percent of travellers are considering this category for summer or autumn. A cooler, calmer alternative to busy beach resorts and a genuine upsell for the right client.
- Multi-generational travel is now a distinct booking pattern. Villas, connecting suites, clustered cruise cabins are three formats worth having ready for families travelling across households.
The full breakdown of this week's trends is on the blog.

https://janinelovestravel.co.uk/whats-trending-in-travel-smart-value-summer-2026-06-25

item.title: UK travellers are not booking less in 2026. They are booking more carefully.
item.description:
UK travellers are not booking less in 2026. They are booking more carefully.
Four trends our agents are drawing on this week:
- 42% of travellers are booking earlier to lock in value; 40% are choosing off-peak timing (Criteo 2026) - Scandinavia and cooler-climate destinations are growing fast… Scandinavia bookings tipped to rise up to 35% this year - The "one big trip" pattern is gaining ground… 12 to 14 night escapes, twin-centres, and long-haul bucket-list itineraries are the shape clients are asking for - Travellers browse 25 hotel listings on average before deciding… a structured three-option quote is the most effective response
Helping clients be smart with their timing and their money is where great agent relationships are built. The full trend breakdown is on the JLT blog this week.
